periods.public: The participants introduce their priorities for the investigation. They discuss the need to balance operational capacity, historical data, and financial transparency.

lines.Asuka: Suggests looking into staffing and maintenance capacity.
lines.Takumi: Proposes checking actual travel times and crowd data.
lines.Benjamin: Mentions the need to see the capital ledger and contractor fees.
lines.Servas: Advocates for reviewing past pilots and accessibility records.
lines.Jonathan: Requests information on committee minutes and station shell contingencies.

lines.Asuka: Agrees with the need for data on crew establishment.
lines.Takumi: Asks if journey audits are available.
lines.Benjamin: Questions the long-term cost of current contracts.
lines.Servas: Reminds the group about the value of closure reports.
lines.Jonathan: Points out the risk of hidden site conditions.

lines.Asuka: Confirms her selection of roster books and crew establishment.
lines.Takumi: Confirms his selection of timed runs and journey audits.
lines.Benjamin: Confirms his selection of capital ledger and contractor fees.
lines.Servas: Confirms his selection of two pilots and accessibility records.
lines.Jonathan: Confirms his selection of committee minutes and contingency pricing.

periods.public: Participants share the implications of their findings without revealing the full text. They debate the feasibility of different types of interventions based on staffing, budget, and historical success.

lines.Asuka: Warns that some staffing pools are dangerously thin.
lines.Takumi: Notes that waiting times are the primary issue, not transit speed.
lines.Benjamin: Highlights a discrepancy between available grants and operating subsidies.
lines.Servas: Mentions that a previous late-night trial was successful.
lines.Jonathan: Warns about high risks and costs in old station structures.

lines.Asuka: Asks @Benjamin if the budget allows for new hiring.
lines.Takumi: Questions @Servas on the scale of the previous pilots.
lines.Benjamin: Explains that funds are ring-fenced for construction, not operations.
lines.Servas: Clarifies that the late-night pilot met cost targets.
lines.Jonathan: Mentions that some administrative consents are already in place.

lines.Asuka: Points out that maintenance contracts have some spare capacity.
lines.Takumi: Argues that ticketing queues are not the main bottleneck.
lines.Benjamin: Notes that contractor fees are eating into the paving budget.
lines.Servas: Observes that some previous lane-priority projects failed.
lines.Jonathan: Notes a lack of agreement on data terms between operators.

periods.public: The group evaluates the candidates against the discovered constraints. They weigh the risk of construction delays against the need for operational efficiency and budget adherence.

lines.Asuka: Analyzes the candidates based on crew availability.
lines.Takumi: Evaluates the candidates based on passenger time savings.
lines.Benjamin: Assesses the candidates based on the capital ledger.
lines.Servas: Compares the candidates to historical outcomes.
lines.Jonathan: Considers the candidates based on delivery risks.

lines.Asuka: Argues for the option that utilizes existing maintenance capacity.
lines.Takumi: Argues for the option that addresses the late-night demand.
lines.Benjamin: Supports the option that fits the ring-fenced construction budget.
lines.Servas: Supports the option with a proven historical pilot.
lines.Jonathan: Questions the feasibility of the most complex construction.

lines.Asuka: Asks @Jonathan if the station risks are manageable.
lines.Takumi: Asks @Asuka if the late-night rosters can be filled.
lines.Benjamin: Suggests the most fiscally sound construction path.
lines.Servas: Reminds the group of the cost-recovery success of the pilot.
lines.Jonathan: Admits that while risky, the construction is funded.

seats.Benjamin: Focuses on the long-term financial commitments and the source of funding. He evaluates candidates based on whether they align with available capital grants.
seats.Jonathan: Focuses on the hidden risks of implementation and administrative hurdles. He weighs the likelihood of delays against the potential benefits.
seats.Servas: Focuses on institutional memory and the results of past attempts. He looks for evidence of previous success to guide the current choice.
seats.Takumi: Focuses on the actual experience of the passenger and time efficiency. He analyzes candidates based on their impact on total journey time.
seats.Asuka: Focuses on the availability of personnel to execute and maintain the plan. She examines the impact on existing rosters and crew capacity.
